title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Manufacturing
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Citrix confirms two actively exploited NetScaler zero-days, CVSS 9.5, now added to CISA’s KEV catalog
items.content_text: Citrix confirmed on 27 September that two NetScaler ADC and Gateway vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (CVSS 9.5 each), are being actively exploited on unmitigated appliances. CVE-2026-88771 is an unauthenticated, improper input-validation flaw that lets an attacker run arbitrary commands in any default configuration; CVE-2026-88772 is a memory-overflow flaw reachable through DTLS, which is enabled by default on VPN virtual servers. Citrix shipped fixes the same day in versions 14.1-73.37 and 13.1-64.23, alongside six more flaws (CVE-2026-88773 through -88778, CVSS 7.0–9.3) disclosed but not reported exploited. CISA added both exploited CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 27 September with a federal deadline of 30 September. NetScaler Gateway is a common front door for contractor, vendor and remote-engineer access into manufacturing DMZs, and Citrix warns that exploitation predating disclosure means patching alone cannot rule out prior compromise.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Citrix security bulletin CTX697096, 27 Sep 2026 (primary); CISA KEV catalog, 27 Sep 2026
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Exploited pre-disclosure; confirmed and patched 27 Sep 2026

items.title: Microsoft: a ransomware affiliate rotating Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT has hit critical manufacturing and chemicals
items.content_text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published a profile on 24 September of Storm-2570, a ransomware affiliate it has tracked since April 2025 that deploys Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis or BERT while its hands-on tradecraft stays the same. Affected organizations are in the US, Canada, the UK, Spain, the Netherlands and Puerto Rico, across 14 sectors that include critical manufacturing, chemicals, energy, and food and agriculture; Microsoft names no victims and gives no count. How the group gets in “remains unconfirmed.” Once inside, it uses remote-management tools (Atera, ScreenConnect, Splashtop, NinjaRMM, MeshAgent), PsExec, Impacket and NetExec to move laterally, Mimikatz, LaZagne and ntdsutil to harvest credentials, and Rclone or s5cmd to take data out. Qilin and DragonForce are the first- and fourth-most-active ransomware groups against manufacturers this year in Black Kite’s count.
tags: Ransomware — Multi-brand affiliate tradecraft, initial access unconfirmed

items.title: Boston Scientific confirms an attacker reached an external-facing network device and halted manufacturing for weeks; SCADA systems were not touched
items.content_text: Boston Scientific disclosed on 26 August that a threat actor had gained access to an external-facing network device and a limited part of its on-premises IT environment, forcing it to halt product manufacturing and queue orders for days while it restored core business systems. In a 22 September update, the medical-device maker said CrowdStrike’s investigation found no evidence the actor reached manufacturing-maintenance systems, product or software development, medical-device maintenance, or SCADA environments, and no data was staged or exfiltrated from those systems. The company has not said whether the incident will materially affect 2026 results. The case is a reminder that an IT-side compromise of a single internet-facing device can stop a production line even when engineering and control systems are never touched.
tags: Incident — Confirmed breach disrupted manufacturing; no SCADA/OT compromise found

_otthreatfeed.category: Incident — Confirmed breach disrupted manufacturing; no SCADA/OT compromise found

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Incident began 25 Aug 2026; recovery update 22 Sep 2026

items.title: Three clusters are exploiting Cisco’s firewall manager; one uses tactics Talos says match Qilin ransomware affiliates
items.content_text: Cisco Talos, in an analysis published 9 September and last updated 21 September, describes three clusters exploiting two flaws in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center: CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0), which lets an unauthenticated attacker run scripts as root and is in CISA’s KEV catalog, and CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3), which lets a remote attacker log in with a low-privileged account. UAT-12197, which Talos describes as crimeware, used CVE-2026-20079. UAT-11823 used both flaws and deployed Cyclops Blink; Talos says its tooling overlaps with the Sandworm APT actor. UAT-11988, a ransomware operator whose tactics Talos calls consistent with Qilin affiliates, used CVE-2026-20316. Talos names no victims or sectors, and no new development has been reported as of 28 September. FMC often manages the firewalls between corporate IT and plant-floor networks.
tags: Exploitation campaign — Cisco Secure FMC, CISA KEV

_otthreatfeed.category: Exploitation campaign — Cisco Secure FMC, CISA KEV

items.title: Check Point’s management-server zero-day and gateway VPN flaw are both exploited, and the KEV deadline has passed
items.content_text: CISA added two exploited Check Point flaws to KEV on 22 September with a 25 September federal deadline, now passed. CVE-2026-93616, a pre-authentication path traversal in Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Management, Log Server and SmartEvent, lets an unauthenticated attacker upload and run scripts; Check Point says it was exploited as a zero-day in a handful of pinpointed attacks on 23 July. CVE-2026-85102, an improper certificate-validation flaw, allows unauthenticated remote code execution on Security Gateways and Spark firewalls running site-to-site or remote-access VPN; fixes shipped on 9 September and an exploitation wave was seen from 12 September. Together they cover the gateways that terminate contractor and integrator VPNs into plant networks and the consoles that set policy between IT and OT.
tags: Incident — Exploited VPN and management-server flaws, CISA KEV

_otthreatfeed.category: Incident — Exploited VPN and management-server flaws, CISA KEV
_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog, 22 Sep 2026 (primary); Check Point sk1000117
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Exploited in targeted attacks on 23 Jul (CVE-2026-93616) and 12 Sep (CVE-2026-85102); KEV listing and deadline 22–25 Sep 2026

items.title: Red Heron stole SCADA/HMI source code from a Taiwanese automation vendor’s own code server
items.content_text: Acronis’s Threat Research Unit reported on 13 September that an actor it tracks as Red Heron exploited CVE-2026-60004, a critical remote-code-execution flaw in self-hosted Gitea, against 11 confirmed targets in five countries (Canada, the US, Taiwan, Argentina and Sri Lanka), deploying a new Linux rootkit Acronis calls SIXZUT. A Taiwanese industrial-automation firm lost code for a SCADA/HMI tool, a surveillance and monitoring product, IoT integrations and a network sniffer — the kind of intellectual property that ends up in products sold to plants worldwide. Acronis attributes the activity, at moderate confidence, to a Chinese-speaking actor operating in a PRC-linked context. Gitea’s fix has been available since 27 July; no new development has been reported as of 28 September.
tags: Threat Intelligence — Supplier source-code theft via a self-hosted code server

items.title: Manufacturing ransomware victims topped 1,183 through July, already ahead of all of 2024
items.content_text: Black Kite’s Manufacturing & Distribution Ransomware Report, published 18 September, counts 1,183 manufacturing ransomware victims globally from January through July 2026, up 39.7% year over year and already past 2024’s full-year total. Nearly half of these incidents came from groups that were absent in 2023 and 2024. European victims grew 85.4%, cutting the US share of victims from 52.3% to 34.8%; Germany alone rose more than 83%. Qilin (178 incidents), The Gentlemen (142), Akira (96), DragonForce (70) and INC Ransom (65) lead the field, and companies with $10–100 million in annual revenue made up 70.2% of manufacturing victims.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Black Kite, 18 Sep 2026 (primary), reported by Industrial Cyber

items.title: IO-Link masters from three vendors share 20 flaws; Nozomi shows how they chain to root on a Pepperl+Fuchs unit
items.content_text: CERT@VDE published three advisories on 16 September (VDE-2026-014, -027 and -028) covering Pepperl+Fuchs, Phoenix Contact and Carlo Gavazzi IO-Link master modules that share the same set of 20 CVEs, CVE-2026-27546 through CVE-2026-27565. Two are rated CVSS v3.1 9.8: CVE-2026-27546, an authentication bypass, and CVE-2026-27565, a malicious IODD upload. On 24 September Nozomi Networks Labs published a technical write-up of the Pepperl+Fuchs findings on an ICE2-8IOL-K45P-RJ45 master, covering 19 of the CVEs — most of them OS command injection — and showing that, chained, they give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device and the ability to manipulate sensor and actuator data. IO-Link masters sit at the field layer of EtherNet/IP and PROFINET lines. No exploitation has been reported.
tags: Advisory — Shared field-I/O flaw set, 20 CVEs, no known exploitation

_otthreatfeed.category: Advisory — Shared field-I/O flaw set, 20 CVEs, no known exploitation

items.title: Schneider’s Modicon M580, a mainstay of process manufacturing, has a critical authentication flaw (CVSS v4.0 9.2)
items.content_text: Schneider Electric disclosed CVE-2026-3869 in security notice SEVD-2026-251-04 on 8 September: an incorrectly implemented authentication algorithm (CWE-303) in Modicon M580 controllers below application level 4.00 and M580 Safety controllers below application level 4.20. It is rated CVSS v4.0 9.2 (v3.1 9.8). The M580 line is widely deployed in process manufacturing, including chemical, pharmaceutical and food-processing lines. An attacker needs network access to the controller; no exploitation has been reported.
tags: Advisory — Controller authentication bypass, no known exploitation

items.title: CISA and the FBI tell operators to rein in third-party ICS integrators after a 2025 integrator breach exposed customer SCADA files
items.content_text: CISA and the FBI released a joint fact sheet, “Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators,” dated 23 September and publicised 24 September. It cites a March–April 2025 compromise of a US industrial automation company in which foreign actors searched for “customers” and “SCADA” and staged about 800 files of customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics for exfiltration. The agencies urge operators to write security requirements into integrator contracts, apply least privilege, route remote access through monitored, logged and preferably on-demand paths, get a full inventory of what the integrator supplied, and practise manual operation in case the integrator itself is compromised. The sheet names power utilities and transportation among the victim’s customers, not manufacturers, but plants routinely give OEMs, machine builders and integrators standing access to PLCs, robots and MES interfaces. Separately, NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Rev. 4, its Guide to OT Security, on 21 September; comments are due 30 November.
tags: Guidance — Third-party ICS integrators; NIST OT security guide draft

_otthreatfeed.category: Guidance — Third-party ICS integrators; NIST OT security guide draft
